name: Wil-Clair Sheet Metal

about:
Wil-Clair Sheet Metal was founded in 1999 in Kansas City, Missouri, by John Svetlecic after he left a previous sheet metal shop following a disagreement over company direction. He brought along two former employees, David Ogle to handle finances and Allen Kubicki to run the shop floor, both of whom remain with the company today. The business started modestly, with first-year revenue around $100,000, but grew steadily; by 2016 annual sales reached nearly $4.5 million, accompanied by multiple facility expansions and a growing headcount.

The shop specializes in custom sheet metal fabrication, offering five-axis waterjet cutting (on an Omax Maxiem 1530), fiber laser cutting, certified welding, metal rolling, press brake forming, plasma cutting, and tile cutting. It also provides engineering and drawing services to develop economical designs. The facility has expanded over the years to accommodate increased capacity, though specific square footage and annual part volumes are not disclosed.

Wil-Clair serves a diverse industrial base including food processing (Kellogg’s, Tyson), commercial signage (Procter & Gamble), plumbing and mechanical contracting (Stine-Nichols Plumbing), construction and entertainment (Worlds of Fun), and general industrial fabrication (CDI, Impact Fabrication). Customers range from large national brands to local design-build firms.

The company emphasizes a problem-solving approach dubbed the “Blacksmith Sheet Metal methodology,” with CEO John Svetlecic stating, “We’ll do whatever it takes to get the job done for our clients.” Differentiators include direct access to leadership—calls are often answered by the CEO, shop superintendent, or foreman—a team of experienced craftsmen, and investment in modern equipment such as five-axis waterjet and fiber laser technology.
